title: An EmDash Content API read reuses its source rows while the site database is unchanged, and any watched write or an unwatched table reads fresh
steps: S1: From the checkout run: node --test packages/cms/tracy-emdash-theme-business/tests/content-api-cache.test.mjs
S2: Read the pass/fail counts and the four tests named below.
expect: A second read with the same change key makes no native list or GET call; a listing over kept rows projects no record again and an id read projects only its own record.
Answers over kept rows equal the per-entry scan byte for byte for listings, filters, maxBytes cuts, cursors and id reads, in three scopes and caller rights.
Writes to content rows, revisions, SEO, bylines, media, options, fields and an ALTER change the key; token use, redirect state, the media-usage index, the scheduler stamp and FTS do not.
A new table, a dropped trigger or a trigger that counts nothing gives a null key (read fresh) until identity-sqlite.mjs runs again; a recreated counter row has a new nonce.

selectors.function: packages/cms/tracy-emdash-theme-business/tools/content-api/reader.mjs cachedRows, changeKey, changesWatched, envelope; tools/content-api/identity-sqlite.mjs migrateIdentity

evidence: Issue #252: each one-id read projected the whole site in the site's only Node process (about 3 s on dev, 2,027 native calls on the Business seed), so a 41-record locate snapshot pegged the site for 128 s.
fence: The change key read in the read's own transaction (identity-sqlite counting triggers, schema cookie, trigger coverage) decides whether kept rows may answer.

tests: the second read takes the kept rows: no native call, no record projected again
answers over kept rows are byte-identical to fresh ones
a write wherever a native read looks changes the key; routine bookkeeping does not
a table without its triggers reads fresh until the identity tool runs again
